newsitem.title: FRANCE: Workers disrupt flights at Toulouse airport.
newsitem.headline: Workers disrupt flights at Toulouse airport.

text.p: Air France Europe flights out of Toulouse-Blagnac airport were significantly disrupted on Thursday as mechanics struck against plans to merge technical operations with Air France from April 1.
Airport officials said the strikers downed tools at 6 a.m. (0500 GMT) on Thursday, provoking a two-hour delay of the day's first flight, bound for Paris.
Several other flights were cancelled or delayed due to the action, the officials said.

Also on Thursday, Belgian employees from French carmaker Renault's plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium, left a new car depot near the northern city of Lille they had been occupying to head for another assembly plant, the Maubeuge Construction Automobile plant, union sources said.
They plan another job action at Maubeuge, which employs 2,500 workers and works on a new Renault model, the X76.

The workers had been in the plant near Lille since March 20, when they impounded about 1,800 new cars as "hostages" to try to stop Renault from closing its Vilvoorde plant and shedding nearly 2,800 jobs.
Renault has said the decision to close the plant is irrevocable.
